claims.claim: Norfloxacin, the closest structural analog sharing the N-ethyl pyridone carboxylic acid 4-oxo core, has measured human oral bioavailability of 30-40% (C05, C08, C15, C16), fasting-state systemic availability estimated at 22-60% with mean 40% (C14), and 35-45% in another report (C23), all above the 20% threshold.

Ofloxacin and levofloxacin, quinolone analogs with the same core, show absolute oral bioavailability approaching or virtually 100% in healthy volunteers (C10, C22), about 100% systemic availability in fasted subjects (C06), and 80-95% in cystic fibrosis patients (C11).

Norfloxacin bioavailability is species-dependent, with limited oral bioavailability in ruminants (C21), but human values remain 30-45%, so the ruminant observation does not contradict the human threshold-relevant outcome.

evidence_gaps: No direct measured oral bioavailability exists for the exact query molecule.
No record covers a bis-carboxylic acid quinolone analog without a basic amine; the closest analogs are zwitterionic mono-acids.
Transporter-mediated absorption for this dianionic structure is unverified.
Food effect and formulation influence on the query are unknown.
Species-dependent quinolone bioavailability (ruminant norfloxacin limited, C21) may not reflect human absorption.
content.decision_summary: Level-2 quinolone-context records reinforce the level-1 decision: ofloxacin absolute bioavailability is virtually 100% when fasted (C22) and norfloxacin is 35-45% (C23), both above the 20% threshold for the closest structural family. The query's extra carboxylic acid and absent basic amine create genuine uncertainty, but no affirmative evidence supports F below 20%; the physicochemical prior alone is insufficient to predict low. Prediction remains high with moderate confidence.
